title: I Thought It Was Just Me

questions.q: How does Brene Brown define shame?
a: The belief you are not good enough to belong
A temporary feeling of embarrassment
A fear of being physically alone
A reaction to unfair criticism
questions.why: Lesson 1 defines shame as the belief that a shortcoming will keep you from acceptance.

questions.q: What is a productive first step to understand shame?
a: Recall past moments and define it yourself
Read every book written about it
Ask others to describe your flaws
Avoid situations that trigger it
questions.why: Lesson 1 suggests thinking back to times you felt shame and using them to define the feeling.

a: Seeing why things happen as they happen
Criticizing yourself harshly
Ignoring your emotions
Analyzing other people's motives
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes critical awareness as observing yourself and the context in the moment.

questions.q: What does critical awareness let you do?
a: Pause and see the bigger picture in time
Prove that you were right
Avoid all difficult conversations
Suppress the feeling permanently
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the pause lets you consider context and address shame directly.

questions.q: What does the summary say about anger?
a: It is a tempting but wrong outlet for shame
It is the healthiest response to shame
It always signals someone else's fault
It should never be felt at all
questions.why: Lesson 3 says anger feels relieving in the moment but leaves you feeling worse.
